approved: AI Kill Switch and Data Centre Control Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
as explained in the linked explanatory memorandum
This bill would require providers of covered advanced AI systems to maintain ways to restrict, suspend or shut them down.
It would introduce incident reporting and ministerial emergency directions when serious harm is threatened.
It would also pause new AI data centres and major expansions until Parliament legislates the required safeguards and expressly ends the moratorium.
Requires technical controls that allow covered AI systems to be restricted or stopped.
Requires critical incidents to be reported and permits emergency directions, subject to reasons, reconsideration and parliamentary reporting.
Prohibits construction of new AI data centres and major expansions while the moratorium operates.
Makes ending the moratorium depend on legislation addressing farmland, water, utility prices, environmental and health protection, community consent and AI safety oversight.
Applies monitoring, investigation and civil enforcement mechanisms to the framework.
Providers of covered AI technologies, data-centre developers, regulators and communities affected by proposed facilities are affected.
